subject: Operations
title: The Denver Airport Baggage System
description: A 60-second lesson on The Denver Airport Baggage System.

hook.text: Denver International Airport delayed opening 16 months because of an automated baggage system that shredded luggage.

buildup.text: The airport planned a fully automated underground baggage system—26 miles of track and 4,000 telecars.

discovery.text: The system was wildly complex. Bags flew off carts, jammed at intersections, and were destroyed by the machinery.

twist.text: Engineers warned it was too ambitious. But the project was too far along to stop—sunk cost fallacy in action.

climax.text: The delay cost $500 million. The automated system was eventually scrapped entirely in favor of a simple conveyor system.

punchline.text: $500 million for a system that was replaced by conveyor belts.

quiz.question: What happened to Denver Airport's automated baggage system?
options: It was scrapped and replaced with conveyors
It was sold to another airport
